title: safeRef path guard is defeated by one leading space, and half its claimed forms are untested
description:
From the 2026-08-02 deep review (MEDIUM, confirmed independently by BOTH passes; the bypass was verified by direct execution of the committed regex).

**The defect.** TASK-175 item 4 added read-steering hardening: `kb_graph_query` nulls an unsafe `ref` before returning it, because `orchestrator-routing` SKILL.md explicitly instructs agents to auto-follow a node's `ref` as a path.

```
const UNSAFE_REF_RE = /^[/\\~]|^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9+.-]*:|(?:^|[/\\])\.\.(?:[/\\]|$)/;
```

The absolute-path, home-shorthand and scheme checks are `^`-anchored, and `safeRef` performs no trimming. Verified by direct execution of the committed regex — every one of these is ALLOWED through:

- `" /etc/passwd"` (single leading space)
- `"\t/etc/passwd"` (tab)
- `"  ~/.ssh/id_rsa"`
- `" \\\\evil-host\\share\\payload"` (UNC path — an SMB credential-leak vector on Windows)
- `"a\n/etc/passwd"`
- `"%2e%2e/x"` (percent-encoded traversal — not covered by the pattern at all)

A single leading space defeats the entire control, while the value still resolves as the intended path for any consumer that trims it. The write side is deliberately unvalidated (`GRAPH_SCHEMA` has `ref: {type: 'string', minLength: 1}`), so nothing upstream prevents such a ref being stored in `knowledge/graph/graph.json`.

**Second defect — the control is mostly untested.** The only spec exercising `safeRef` (`tests/e2e/kb-graph-query.spec.js`) feeds exactly three inputs: `../../etc/passwd`, `/etc/passwd`, `https://evil.example/x`. Mutation-confirmed: deleting `~` from the first character class, deleting `\\` from it, or deleting the `(?:^|[/\\])` mid-path prefix each leaves the ENTIRE suite green while re-opening `~/secrets`, `\\host\share`, and `docs/../../etc/passwd` respectively. Only the drive-letter case is incidentally covered, because it rides the same scheme alternation as the https input.

**Third item — the suppression is invisible at the consumption point.** `safeRef` introduces a `ref: null` value that `GRAPH_SCHEMA` says is impossible (ref is a required non-empty string). The `kb_graph_query` tool description still documents output as `{ query, source, nodes }` with no mention that `ref` can be null, and `orchestrator-routing` SKILL.md — edited in the very same diff — still tells agents to follow `ref` without noting the nulled case. An agent told to follow `ref` receives `null` with no explanation.

**Scope note:** keep this at the READ boundary as TASK-175 deliberately scoped it. Hardening `GRAPH_SCHEMA` on the write side is a genuine trust-boundary change and is explicitly OUT of scope here — if the work argues for it, raise it as a separate ticket rather than widening this one.
acceptance_criteria: A failing spec first reproduces the bypass: refs with leading whitespace (space, tab, newline) preceding an absolute path, a ~ home shorthand, or a UNC \\host\share path are currently returned UNCHANGED by safeRef. Capture the red-run output verbatim as the tests-first evidence.

safeRef normalizes before matching (or the pattern is rewritten) so leading and trailing whitespace cannot defeat the guard. All six forms named in the ticket are blocked: leading-whitespace absolute, tab-prefixed absolute, whitespace + ~ shorthand, UNC \\host\share, embedded-newline absolute, and percent-encoded traversal (%2e%2e).

Every alternation in the pattern is individually locked by a test that fails under mutation. Specifically: deleting ~ from the character class, deleting \\ from it, or deleting the (?:^|[/\\]) mid-path prefix must EACH break at least one test. Prove this by actually running the three mutations and recording the failures in the hand-off.

The ref: null case is documented where it is consumed: the kb_graph_query tool description states that ref may be null and why, and orchestrator-routing SKILL.md (BOTH parity copies, byte-identical) tells agents what to do when ref is null rather than assuming it is always a followable path.

No write-side change: GRAPH_SCHEMA stays as-is and this ticket does not widen into write-boundary validation. Verify with git diff. If the work argues the write side needs hardening, raise it as a separate ticket in the closing comment instead.
npm run test:all is green; no existing kb-graph/mcp spec regresses; dist/mcp-server.cjs rebuilt via npm run build:plugin and committed, with tests/e2e/dist-parity.spec.js passing.

comments.author: orchestrator
comments.body:
CLOSED on a green review. **APPROVE — 0 HIGH / 1 MEDIUM (process) / 4 LOW.** All 6 ACs PASS.

**Review depth: `full`** — rubric inputs: 164 changed lines (>=150) plus two mandatory-FULL surfaces: security surface (input validation at a trust boundary — agents are instructed to auto-follow a node's `ref` as a filesystem path) and packaging/dist (`dist/mcp-server.cjs`).

## All six named bypasses closed, verified by direct execution
The reviewer executed the COMMITTED `safeRef` against each form rather than trusting spec names. `" /etc/passwd"`, `"\t/etc/passwd"`, `"  ~/.ssh/id_rsa"`, `" \\evil-host\share\payload"`, `"a\n/etc/passwd"`, `"%2e%2e/x"` — all return `null`. The red state was independently reproduced from the literal pre-fix guard extracted via `git show`, not hand-transcribed: 6/6 right-reason failures.

## Zero false negatives on live data — the risk that mattered most
A tightened path guard that nulls real refs would be worse than the hole it closes. The reviewer ran **every ref in the real `knowledge/graph/graph.json` through the committed guard: 225 refs, 0 nulled.** Including the `state/sessions/<id>/archive.jsonl#<timestamp>` fragment refs, which survive intact. No live data breaks.

## Adjacent-form hunt (I asked for this explicitly; it found real residuals)
Better than expected in one direction — JS `String.trim()` covers the full Unicode whitespace set, so NBSP, BOM, U+2028, vertical tab and ideographic space are all blocked, as are `%2E%2E` (the `i` flag works), `%2e%2e%2f`, mid-path `%2e%2e`, and schemes behind whitespace.

**Residuals that pass through:** `%252e%252e/x` (double-encoded), `..%2fx`, `..%5cx`, `..%2f..%2fetc%2fpasswd`, `x%2f..%2fetc`, `....//etc/passwd`, `a%00/etc/passwd`. Every one requires a consumer that percent-decodes or naively strips `../` BEFORE resolving, and no such consumer exists — agents open the ref as a literal repo-relative path. So exploitability today is nil. But `..%2fx` is a direct sibling of the `%2e%2e` alternation this ticket just added, and it slips.

## LOW-1 — the docs overclaim, which is the part that actually matters
`SKILL.md:997` and the tool description at `src/mcp-server.js:550` both tell agents the guard covers refs "disguised via ... percent-encoding" WITHOUT qualification. Given the residuals above that is a mild overclaim — and false confidence in a control is precisely the failure class this ticket exists to reduce. The reviewer's suggested arms-race-ending fix for the follow-up: **reject any ref containing `%` outright.** 0 of the 225 live refs contain one, so the false-negative cost is provably zero, and it replaces a token blacklist with a whitelist-shaped rule. Recorded in the follow-up ticket below.

## AC5 follow-up (required by the AC to be recorded here)
The write side stays unvalidated by design: `GRAPH_SCHEMA` in `src/knowledge-graph.js` is untouched (0-line diff, verified twice), so an unsafe ref can still be WRITTEN to `knowledge/graph/graph.json` — it just will not be surfaced to an agent. The reviewer assessed this as **correctly scoped out, not a weakness**: `safeRef` sits at the point of CONSUMPTION, the only place a ref becomes an instruction to open a file, so it is complete as a control regardless of what is stored. Hardening the schema would be defense-in-depth, would be a genuine trust-boundary change, and would break existing graphs at load time. Minted as a separate ticket together with LOW-1.

## AC3 mutation drills, re-run independently
The reviewer extracted the committed regex literally and mutated the pattern text programmatically in a scratchpad (repo never mutated). Deleting `~` from the char class, deleting `\\` from it, and collapsing the mid-path prefix to `^` each break exactly their targeted test. One nuance recorded: deleting the `(?:^|[/\\])` group ENTIRELY makes `\.\.` match anywhere — strictly more permissive-to-block, an over-matching mutation rather than a bypass-introducing one. The security-meaningful weakening is the anchor-only form, and that one is caught.

## Caller coverage
`safeRef` has exactly one production call site (`sortNodesById`'s projection map). All four return paths of `kb_graph_query` traced: id query (both the local-relation and canonical-first branches converge), type-only query, the neither-id-nor-type path (returns `nodes: []`, no refs at all), and the id-existence check that surfaces no ref. **No production path bypasses the guard.** The `export` is not a workaround — the e2e spec still exercises the real MCP round trip and asserts `ref === null` on the wire.

## Gate
`test:since -- 180fa3d` 10 files / 99 passed (non-zero selection) · `npm test` 77 files / 1043 passed, 2 skipped · named e2e 4 files / 52 passed · skill-parity sensor 13 passed · `npm run test:all` 171 files / 1969 passed, 4 skipped · `check:calibration` clean · dist-parity green, `dist/mcp-server.cjs` machine-built with four hunks matching the four source changes.

**Parity:** both `orchestrator-routing/SKILL.md` copies byte-identical, sensor green.

## Remaining LOWs (non-blocking, carried)
The `export` widens the shipped bundle's public surface for a test-only consumer — a conscious debt, justified in-code. The spec header's red-run sequencing depends on an intra-commit export step, so running it verbatim at the true pre-fix tree would fail on `safeRef is not a function`; the sequence used (export, red-run, fix) is legitimate TDD and the reviewer confirmed the right-reason red independently, but a hand-off note naming the intermediate state would remove the ambiguity. And two happy-path tests exercise the same path with the same outcome — defensible as false-negative insurance across two ref shapes.

**MEDIUM (process only):** the five-item pre-hand-off checklist was not forwarded to the reviewer in my briefing. The reviewer verified all five underlying classes independently and found no substantive defect behind it — this is my briefing gap, not a developer omission; the hand-off did state them.
